{"claims":[{"claim_text":"Agriculture has suffered through eight years of the Democrats' regulatory policies, particularly from the Environmental Protection Agency (EPA).",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"States, not Washington bureaucrats, are best equipped to develop sound farm oversight policies.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Environmental Protection Agency (EPA)'s Waters of the United States (WOTUS) rule, issued jointly with the Army Corps of Engineers, is a travesty.",
"claim_types":["evaluation"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Waters of the United States (WOTUS) rule extends the government's jurisdiction over navigable waters into the micro-management of puddles and ditches on farms, ranches, and other privately-held property.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Ditches, dry creek beds, stock ponds, prairie potholes, and other non-navigable wet areas are already regulated by the states.",
"claim_types":["factual_assertion"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"The Waters of the United States (WOTUS) rule is subject to judicial review and must be invalidated.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Unelected bureaucrats must be stopped from furthering the Democratic Party's political agenda through regulatory demands forced upon citizens and businesses beyond that which is required by law.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"Federal agencies must never seize control of state waters, watersheds, or groundwater.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]},{"claim_text":"State waters, watersheds, and groundwater must be the purview of the sovereign states.",
"claim_types":["policy_position"],"evidence_ids":[1]}],"unresolved_references":[]}
```
